title: The Anglo-Zulu War
summary: Britain invaded the Zulu kingdom to bring it into a planned confederation of South Africa. Despite a stunning Zulu victory at Isandlwana, the kingdom was defeated within seven months.
caveat: Unusually well documented: British military reports, soldiers' letters and later Zulu testimony collected by historians. Casualty figures for the Zulu side are estimates.

stops.title: The ultimatum
stops.narration: Under a fig tree on the Thukela River, British officials read terms to King Cetshwayo's envoys that he could not accept, including disbanding his army.
sources: Jeff Guy, The Destruction of the Zulu Kingdom (1979)
John Laband, Kingdom in Crisis: The Zulu Response to the British Invasion of 1879 (1992)

stops.title: Isandlwana
stops.narration: The main Zulu army surprised a British camp beneath this sphinx-shaped hill. More than 1,300 men on the British side were killed, the worst defeat of a British army by an African force.
sources: John Laband, Kingdom in Crisis: The Zulu Response to the British Invasion of 1879 (1992)

stops.title: Rorke's Drift
stops.narration: The invasion had crossed the Buffalo River here. Hours after Isandlwana, about 150 soldiers held the mission station through the night against several thousand Zulu reserves.

stops.title: Hlobane
stops.narration: A British raid on this flat-topped mountain was caught by the arrival of the main Zulu army and routed.
sources: John Laband, Kingdom in Crisis: The Zulu Response to the British Invasion of 1879 (1992)

stops.title: Kambula
stops.narration: The next day, the same Zulu army attacked a fortified British camp and was beaten off with heavy losses. Many historians see this as the turning point.
sources: John Laband, Kingdom in Crisis: The Zulu Response to the British Invasion of 1879 (1992)

stops.title: Gingindlovu
stops.narration: A relief column defeated a Zulu force here and went on to lift the siege of a British garrison at Eshowe.
sources: John Laband, Kingdom in Crisis: The Zulu Response to the British Invasion of 1879 (1992)

stops.title: Ulundi
stops.narration: A British square of infantry, artillery and Gatling guns broke the last major Zulu attack. Cetshwayo's royal homestead at oNdini was burned.
sources: John Laband, Kingdom in Crisis: The Zulu Response to the British Invasion of 1879 (1992)
Jeff Guy, The Destruction of the Zulu Kingdom (1979)

stops.title: Cetshwayo's capture
stops.narration: The king was captured in the Ngome forest and sent into exile. Britain divided the kingdom into 13 chiefdoms, setting off years of civil war.
stops.confidence_note: The exact capture site within the forest area is approximate.
sources: Jeff Guy, The Destruction of the Zulu Kingdom (1979)
